newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week ending Sep 20.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week ending Sep 20.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported an 11.46 percent rise in its turnover during the week ending September 20 amidst a sharp decline in the number of transactions and deteriorating market liquidity.
The total weekly turnover jumped to 36.856 million dinars ($7.37 million) from 33.066 million dinars in the previous week. The number of transactions plunged from 178 to 145.
A new tranche of the central bank 30-day bonds, launched September 9, largely enlivened otherwise slack market activity, grabbing over a half of the weekly turnover, traders said.
The bonds, carrying an annual interest rate of 115.61 percent, were traded twice for a volume of 20 million dinars.
Apart from the bonds, other market segments were hit hard by tightening market liquidity, traders said.
Market liquidity is unusually low after the central bank introduced a 10 percent reserve requirement at the end of August, a trader told Reuters.

"Monetary authorities are trying to drain liquidity from the market, but such a high percentage of the reserve requirement leaves market participants with lack of free funds, pushing up average daily interest rates, particularly in the giro money market -- trading surplus liquidity among banks."
Analysts said the central bank's measure to drain liquidity from the market was too harsh, recalling that the highest percentage of the reserve requirement ever was eight percent.
"This (the reserve requirement) is choking market activity, causing delays in issuers meeting their obligations," another trader said.

Commercial paper segment, with interest rates ranging from an annual 44 to 520 percent, saw 126 transactions totalling 13.926 million dinars, while treasury bills generated 2.380 million dinars in 14 deals.
